transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE); Aisha Patel (Redwood SE); Marcus Nguyen (Redwood Product); Maya Rodriguez (Arbor CTO); Ethan Park (Arbor ML Eng); Priya Singh (Arbor Infra); Samir Joshi (Arbor PM)

Summary (auto-gen): Quick demo of Redwood model catalog and Optimize recommendations for open models. Focus: pick candidate models for Arbor's customer-facing summarization with tight p95 latency targets.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Liam, AE on this account. quick intros?
[00:08] Maya Rodriguez (Arbor): Maya here, CTO. we own the overall infra and sec decisioning.
[00:12] Ethan Park (Arbor): Ethan, I run the ML infra and prototyping.
[00:15] Priya Singh (Arbor): Priya, infra/ops, VPC and keys.
[00:19] Samir Joshi (Arbor): Samir—product, will drive use cases.
[00:22] Aisha Patel (Redwood): Aisha, systems SE, I will demo the catalog and bench logic.
[00:27] Marcus Nguyen (Redwood): Marcus from product, quick note on the Optimize heuristics.
[00:31] Liam: Great. high-level agenda: show catalog filters, walk through a bench result CSV, interpret compatibility matrix (which kernels and quantization are safe), and then map to pilot ask — dedicated with VPC peering.
[00:45] Maya: Sounds good. Our constraints: 200ms p95 for 1k token sessions is ideal but we can be flexible to 300ms if cost tradeoffs are acceptable. Data residency: EU-only for regulated customers; but pilot can be US. SOC2 plus SSO is mandatory.
[01:10] Liam: Noted. we'll flag SOC2 docs in the follow up. quick question on volume: expected sustained QPS?
[01:18] Ethan: For the pilot we expect around 15 qps, bursty to 60 during peak. steady-state for prod potentially 200 qps across shards.
[01:28] Aisha: That's helpful. Okay i'll share the console — i'm switching to catalog view now, apologies if the screen blurs as i alt-tab.
[01:38] [screen share: redwood console — model catalog]
[01:42] Aisha: So this is our curated open-model catalog. you can filter by family, sequence length, tokenization compat, and importantly by our bench profile which we run across hardware targets. i'm going to apply a filter: models under 32k context and optimized for low-latency.
[02:05] Samir: can you show the bench columns? what metrics do you report?
[02:09] Aisha: Sure — by default we show median latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, cost-per-infer (unit), and a quality score from our eval harness. note that p95 includes a typical prefix cache behavior where KV cache hits reduce latency. for novel cold calls p99 might be worse.
[02:28] Ethan: Is the quality score comparable across architectures? Bimodal stuff can be tricky.
[02:33] Aisha: We normalize scores per task family — summarization in this case — using our eval set. it's not perfect but it's a quick filter. we recommend picking a short list and running a customer prompt sweep.
[02:45] [05:00] Aisha: i'll open an example bench CSV from a previous sprint — (shared: bench-results-arbor-sim.csv). Notice the platform columns: hw_type (A100-80GB, L40s, H100), kernel_tag, quantization (int8, fp16), median_ms, p95_ms, tk_per_s.
[05:25] Ethan: quick q — kernel_tag, is that like the compiled kernel set?
[05:28] Aisha: Yes. kernel_tag is our internal label for the compilation + runtime path that gave the measurement. It maps to specific attention kernels, fused ops, and memory layout. that's important because some models will fallback to slower kernels on certain hw or sequence lengths.
[05:48] Marcus: Also worth noting, Optimize suggests kernel/quantization combos based on your target SLO and the sequence length histogram. we'll run a simulated sweep on your prompt set to recommend batch sizes and whether int8 is safe.
[06:04] Priya: How safe is int8 for hallucination-prone tasks?
[06:08] Aisha: It depends. for many summarization tasks int8 with per-channel calibration keeps quality within a few points, but for legal/PII sensitive outputs we recommend fp16 for the pilot until we validate eval metrics.
[06:22] Maya: So what's the typical cost delta between fp16 and int8?
[06:25] Marcus: On average 25-40% cheaper on token cost due to improved throughput, but again depends on batch and sequence length.
[06:33] [08:00] Aisha: i'll filter to only open-source LLAMA-family variants we have verified. here are three candidates: llm-xsmall-7b-q, phoenix-13b-fp16, and atlas-30b-quant. each has a compatibility badge — green, amber, red — indicating recommended vs partial support.
[08:52] Ethan: Atlas-30b looks promising for quality but p95 is higher on A100, is that a kernel issue?
[08:58] Aisha: yes, atlas uses a family of attention ops that on older kernels fall back to a slower path. that's why the compatibility matrix shows amber for A100-80GB, but green on H100 with our optimized kernels.
[09:12] Samir: Can we pin a fallback policy so if the optimized kernel isn't available we go to a smaller model to meet p95?
[09:17] Aisha: Absolutely. The routing policy UI allows priority rules: prefer model A on region x with kernel tag y, otherwise route to model B or Dedicated pool. We'll demo that after benches.
[09:30] Liam: quick aside — competitors like Anthropic offer simple model tiers but not this level of kernel-to-hardware mapping or automatic fallback that preserves SLOs. you should weigh that.
[09:43] Maya: Good to know. show us a concrete bench row and how you'd interpret for our 200ms target.
[09:50] Aisha: Opening the CSV row for llm-xsmall-7b-q on L40s: median 48ms, p95 110ms for 512 tokens, tokens/sec 1600, cost unit $0.0009. For 1k tokens p95 scales roughly +30-40% due to decoding length. so rough p95 would be ~150ms — within your 200ms.
[10:24] Ethan: The burst to 60 qps — what's the batching behavior? will we see latency cliffs?
[10:29] Aisha: Our runtime uses continuous batching with adaptive slice sizing; in Dedicated you can reserve GPU pools to keep cold start low. we also do prefix caching so repeated prefixes or system prompts are cached in KV to reduce compute. spikes beyond reserved pool will enqueue but we have priority lanes for paid bursts.
[10:48] Priya: VPC peering — do we need to open specific ports? KMS integration?
[10:52] Liam: We support VPC peering and also private deploy with customer-managed control plane. KMS/HSM integration is via standard KMS APIs; i'll include the KMS runbook in the follow up.
[11:06] [15:00] Aisha: Back to kernel mapping: here's a compatibility matrix view — rows are models, columns are hw targets and quant modes; green means full support with optimized kernels, amber means partial (fall back for long sequences), red means not recommended. you can export this table as a JSON or CSV.
[15:33] Marcus: The Optimize panel suggests a shortlist based on your SLO and cost weight. for example, if you weigh latency=0.7 and cost=0.3, optimize recommends llm-xsmall-7b-q on L40s int8, with a canary rollout to atlas-30b for higher-quality but slower paths.
[15:55] Samir: Can we automate rollouts? say 5% traffic to atlas then 20% then scale?
[15:59] Aisha: Yes — rollout policies support canary percentages, A/B, and automatic rollback if latency or quality regressions cross thresholds. Quality regressions are tied to eval prompt sets you provide.
[16:20] Maya: On audit — do we keep per-request logs and token-level attribution? we need them for compliance.
[16:25] Liam: We emit request traces and per-token consumption metrics; you can opt into longer retention with our enterprise logs addon. SSO/SAML is supported and RBAC can lock model editing to certain groups.
[16:40] Ethan: Is there a demo environment we can run our prompt set against without spinning a full pilot?
[16:44] Aisha: We provide a sandbox with limited quotas and a bench runner. you can upload your prompt set and run a simulated bench; results map into the same compatibility and Optimize recommendations. this is what we'll do in the pilot pre-work.
[17:00] [22:00] Aisha: i'll trigger a live bench run for one prompt from your sample — using llm-xsmall-7b-q on L40s int8 — starting now, this will take a couple minutes.
[24:20] Aisha: bench finished, attaching the quick view: median 42ms p95 112ms for 256-token queries. note warm cache trick — first-token latency a bit higher.
[24:40] Ethan: Seems good. what about threading with long context 8k?
[24:44] Aisha: for 8k we recommend a higher-memory hw and different kernels; Optimize says atlas-30b-fp16 on H100 gives best quality but p95 increases ~2.2x compared to short context. that's expected.
[25:10] Priya: For pilot we want to ensure keys never leave our KMS. can Redwood integrate with AWS KMS/HSM?
[25:18] Liam: yes, we have KMS integrations; for private deployments we can also support customer-managed HSM. i'll share integration notes.
[25:40] [30:00] Marcus: i'll quickly show the Console flow to create a pilot: select models, create a Dedicated pool profile, pin kernel_tag and quantization, set rollout policy and SLOs, and add evaluation prompts for quality monitoring. then you can enable alerts for regression.
[31:10] Samir: If we want to start with hosted for speed and then move to Dedicated, is that pain-free?
[31:15] Aisha: It's seamless — same API and model names. the only changes are routing and capacity. you can start hosted, then when you're ready, perform a switch to Dedicated and pin the same model versions.
[31:30] Maya: What about model versioning? we need pinned model hashes for audits.
[31:34] Marcus: We provide immutable model version IDs and an artifact manifest; you can freeze a version and any rollout references it by hash.
[31:45] Ethan: Any known compatibility surprises with open models—like unexpected tokenizer differences?
[31:50] Aisha: Tokenizers can vary; we surface tokenization mismatches and warn if prefix tokens blow out context. we also provide tokenizer normalization helpers.
[32:05] [38:00] Aisha: Recap — shortlist: llm-xsmall-7b-q (primary), atlas-30b-fp16 (fallback for quality); plan: Arbor uploads 3 prompt sets, Redwood runs bench and returns a kernel mapping CSV and suggested rollout config; pilot: 30 days on Dedicated with VPC peering, SOC2 docs exchanged and SSO configured.
[32:32] Maya: That sounds right. questions from my side — what SLAs do we get on Dedicated?
[32:36] Liam: Standard Dedicated SLA is 99.95% with latency targets configurable per pool; will include in pricing doc.
[32:44] Priya: Any network egress patterns we should be aware of?
[32:47] Aisha: For hosted, model binaries live in our secured infra; traffic goes over the peered VPC or TLS depending on mode. will include the network diagram.
[32:58] Ethan: Can you provide an example rollout JSON? we'd like to feed it into our infra-as-code.
[33:03] Marcus: Yes, the export is a small JSON/YAML manifest with model IDs, kernel tags, and percentages; i'll attach a sample.
[33:15] Samir: timeline — if we send prompt sets by Monday, when can we see bench results?
[33:19] Aisha: If you send them Monday (2026-06-22) we can run a prioritized bench and return results by Thursday (2026-06-25).
[33:30] Maya: ok copy. Any blockers we haven't discussed?
[33:33] Priya: need to review the KMS/HSM integration doc and confirm peering windows.
[33:38] Liam: we'll include that.
[33:40] [40:00] Closing bits — Liam recapped action items and next meetings: pilot kickoff tentative 2026-06-24, security deep-dive on 2026-06-20.
[40:20] Maya: thanks everyone, this was useful.
[40:25] Ethan: good session.
[40:28] Aisha: thanks all — i'll follow up with the bench CSV and the kernel mapping export.
[40:33] Marcus: i'll attach the sample rollout manifest and pricing tiers.
[40:36] [46:50] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: auto transcription occasionally mislabels kernel_tag as 'kernel tag' or 'carnel tag' and confuses model nicknames; human follow-up recommended for quoted IDs.
